title: The Bacteria That Eats Plastic
hook: Could bacteria learn to digest our rubbish?
script: Could bacteria learn to digest our rubbish? In 2016, scientists found Ideonella sakaiensis at a Japanese recycling site, thriving on PET plastic bottles. This bacterium uses two enzymes to transform PET into energy. Despite the efficiency, it relies on a symbiotic relationship with other microbes. Its enzyme action is as efficient as termites digesting wood. Engineered versions can now break a bottle in hours, hinting at a new recycling future. Imagine: plastic waste as a feast for bacteria.
